prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1373; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a left-turn collision at an intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck while turning, and the claimant reports a knee injury from the impact. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it, with coverage in force on the loss date. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Photographs taken at the scene show damage that lines up with the described impact pattern. There are no independent witnesses beyond the parties involved, so the photos are the main visual record.

Entry 4: Police report and statements from responding officers confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. No prior damage to the vehicle has been identified in the records pulled so far.

Entry 5: Claimant's account has been consistent across the recorded call, the written statement, and the follow-up with counsel present. The described knee injury is plausible for a crash of this type and nothing in the medical history shows a prior injury to that body area.

Entry 6: Treatment records show a usual course of care, with visits tapering as the claimant's knee improved over time. The billing matches the treatment documented and no unusual gaps or escalations appear.

Entry 7: Reviewed the file as a whole. Vehicle damage, the police record, the photos, and the medical course are consistent with the reported loss. Claim recommended for standard evaluation of the bodily injury portion with counsel's demand to follow.
